label: Cisco Catalyst 1000 C1000-24FP-4X-L
description: Cisco Catalyst 1000 C1000-24FP-4X-L - 24x 1G RJ-45 all PoE+ (802.3af/at, 30 W a port, 370 W budget), 4x 10G SFP+ uplink cages that also take a 1G SFP, 128 Gbps switching bandwidth, 95.23 Mpps at 64 bytes, fan-cooled 1U Cisco IOS L2 access switch.

poe.note: 370 W PoE budget across 24 PoE+ ports, IEEE 802.3af/802.3at PSE, 30 W maximum a port. Perpetual PoE holds power on the PD across a reload. The budget, not the port count, is the ceiling: 24 Class-3 (15.4 W) PDs or 12 30 W PDs fit (24 x 15.4 W = 369.6 W, 12 x 30 W = 360 W).

notes: Datasheet Table 1 and Table 2: 24 copper ports, 4x 10G SFP+ uplink cages that also take a 1G SFP, 370 W PoE budget, one fan, 34.8 dB sound pressure, 17.48 x 13.59 x 1.73 in deep, 4.6 kg; single internal autoranging 100-240 VAC supply; 95.23 Mpps forwarding rate; 16,000 unicast MAC entries, 256 active VLANs, 4094 VLAN IDs, 64 STP instances, 9198-byte L3 MTU, 10,240-byte jumbo frame. The switching bandwidth is the sum of every port at line rate, so no port group is oversubscribed. RJ-45 console (EIA/TIA-232) at 9600 baud, 8 data bits, 1 stop bit, no parity, no flow control; a USB Type A port takes a FAT-formatted flash drive for image and configuration recovery. Cisco calls the series Layer 2, but Table 2 budgets 542 IPv4 direct and 256 indirect routes (414/128 for IPv6), so static inter-VLAN routing is modelled as l3-forward, not a full L3 feature set. No 802.3bt anywhere in the series: 30 W a port is the ceiling. The four uplink cages are SFP+ and take a 1G SFP as well as a 10G module. Cisco renames the cage with the module: the HIG port-mapping table maps Gi1/0/25-28 to Ten1/0/1-4, and says a 10G module in a 1G slot, or the reverse, needs default-interface run on the mapped port before it carries traffic. The 128 Gbps switching figure covers a 10G module in all four cages; with 1G modules it is 56 Gbps, as on the -4G models.
